Eric has been named "CEO of the Year" at the 2019 Business Excellence Forum, one of the "Top 30 Entrepreneurs in the UK", 35 and under, by Startups Magazine, and among "Britain's Most Disruptive Entrepreneurs" by The Telegraph. His work has featured on over 7 major TV stations, in the Wall Street Journal, and The Economist. He has also appeared as a guest judge on The Apprentice.

Over the last 20 years Eric has advised Fortune 50 CEOs while at McKinsey & Company, helped build Skype’s multi-billion dollar success story, founded several companies, and helped scale over 100.

Eric has completed a coaching certification and apprenticeship with Professor BJ Fogg, who leads Stanford University’s Behavior Design Lab. He also continues to research evidence-based studies in psychology, neuroscience, habit change, leadership, and peak performance.

Eric coaches and mentors founders and CEOs throughout the world. He draws from his world-class work experiences, cutting-edge research, and behavioral science from Stanford University - as well as the approaches and techniques used in the worlds of elite sports and the military - areas where peak performance is key.

Today Eric runs his own investment and advisory firm helping clients scale their companies, their leadership, and themselves. Over 100 companies have been advised and/or invested in to date, ranging from pre-revenue to multi-billion-dollar valuations, with 30 active portfolio companies. Sectors include AI, fintech, quantum computing, digital transformation, point-of-sale solutions, online home furnishings, hospitality tech, outsourced employment solutions, and cybersecurity to name a handful.

As a speaker, Eric is well-positioned to speak about peak performance, leadership, and company building. Over the years he has shared stages with Jesse Itzler, Lord Alan Sugar, Bear Grylls, Stedman Graham, Double Gold Olympic Champion Kelly Holmes, and Stephen M.R. Covey, to name a few.

Eric is also the author of the Amazon best-seller "The 3 Alarms" and is currently working on his next book with Dr. Christian Poensgen.

He also writes Peak Performance Insights - the newsletter that provides ultra-practical tips for business, leadership, and self-mastery.

Learn more at www.EricPartaker.com and join a growing community of over 235,000 people.

For more than 20 years, I have helped manufacturing and logistics organizations improve performance by building stronger operations, developing leaders, and creating systems that deliver sustainable business results.

My career has taken me from the production floor to leading multi-site operational transformations across Europe, the USA, and Turkey. I’ve worked with organizations ranging from local manufacturing plants to global operations, always with the same objective: turning operational complexity into stability, capability, and measurable business performance.

I don’t see Operational Excellence as a department or Lean as a toolbox.

I see them as leadership systems.

The best organizations don’t improve because they have more Lean tools. They improve because their leaders make better decisions, develop better people, solve problems at the root, and build systems that continue improving long after the consultants have left.

Throughout my career I have led operational transformations, developed leadership teams, standardized multi-site operations, implemented Daily Management Systems, improved quality, productivity, safety, customer performance, and cost efficiency, while delivering measurable financial results through operational discipline and continuous improvement.

My leadership philosophy is simple:

People do not fail because they don’t care.
Processes fail because leaders accept systems that make success difficult.

That’s why I spend my time where the work happens.

The Gemba is where assumptions disappear, facts become visible, and the best improvements begin.

I believe leadership is not about controlling people.

It is about creating the conditions where people can succeed.

My work focuses on:

• Multi-site Operations Leadership
• Operational Strategy & Business Transformation
• Operational Excellence & Lean Enterprise
• Manufacturing & Logistics Performance
• Leadership Development & Coaching
• Quality Management & Continuous Improvement
• Daily Management Systems & Performance Management
• Standardization, Problem Solving & Sustainable Change

What drives me most is not implementing another improvement project.

It is leaving behind stronger leaders, stronger systems, and organizations that continue improving long after my work is finished.

If you’re looking for someone who combines operational leadership with hands-on execution, challenges the status quo, and turns complexity into sustainable business performance, I’d be pleased to connect.

items.about:
You just know your product is better than your website makes it look.

You see it on sales calls, in demos or during onboarding, when people finally get the product only after someone from your team explains it properly.

That usually creates a hidden sales problem.

The product still sells, but the team has to do too much explaining because the website cannot carry enough understanding on its own.

Someone lands on the homepage, scans for a minute and tries to answer:

• What is it?
• Who is it for?
• What does it solve?
• What does it replace?
• Why should I care now?

When those answers are not clear, best-fit buyers leave without forming a clear picture of where the product fits in their workflow.

That is the problem I help B2B SaaS teams fix.

I run a 2-week Website Messaging Redo + Homepage Rewrite sprint for SaaS teams that have a strong product, but a website that undersells it.

The sprint builds the messaging foundation first, then turns it into homepage copy.

This usually creates two kinds of clarity:

1. Internal clarity for the team

• clear definition of the best-fit customer
• agreement on the main use case the product is built for
• alignment across marketing, product and sales
• one product story the team can reuse across pages and sales materials

2. External clarity for best-fit buyers

• homepage shows the workflow the product fits into
• buyers quickly recognize the situation the product solves
• the explanation follows a clear sequence
• the next step becomes easier because the product already makes sense

The sprint usually covers:

• ICP clarity
• positioning
• core messaging
• homepage structure 
• full homepage copy

The end result is a homepage that explains the product clearly before buyers sign up, book a demo or talk to sales.

I’ve seen this across 50+ B2B SaaS messaging projects where the product was strong, but the website did not show how it fit into a real buyer workflow.

Once that workflow fit becomes clear, the homepage starts helping buyers understand the product before they ever talk to the team.

If that sounds like your website, send it over and I’ll take a look :)
